title: Sort the intake
briefing: ~/inbox has four files dropped in together: report.pdf, notes.txt, data.csv
and photo.png. Sort them — text files (.txt, .csv) into ~/text, and the
An `if` with a chain of tests would work, but `case` is made for exactly
this: match one value against several patterns and branch.
tips: `case $f in PATTERN) ... ;; PATTERN) ... ;; esac` — patterns are globs, and `a|b` matches either.
Loop the files and branch inside: `for f in *; do case $f in *.txt|*.csv) mv "$f" ~/text/ ;; *) ... ;; esac; done`.
objective: Move every .txt and .csv file from ~/inbox into ~/text, and every .pdf and .png into ~/media. Use a case to decide. Leave ~/inbox empty.
expert_objective: Sort ~/inbox: text (.txt/.csv) to ~/text, media (.pdf/.png) to ~/media, with a case.
hints: Walk the files with a loop, then branch on each name with case: `for f in *; do case $f in ... ; esac; done`.
Text patterns together: `*.txt|*.csv) mv "$f" ~/text/ ;;` — and media: `*.pdf|*.png) mv "$f" ~/media/ ;;`.
`cd ~/inbox`, then `for f in *; do case $f in *.txt|*.csv) mv "$f" ~/text/ ;; *.pdf|*.png) mv "$f" ~/media/ ;; esac; done`
solution:
cd ~/inbox
for f in *; do case $f in *.txt|*.csv) mv "$f" ~/text/ ;; *.pdf|*.png) mv "$f" ~/media/ ;; esac; done
explanation: `case WORD in pattern) ... ;; esac` matches a value against glob patterns, top to bottom, running the first that fits — with `|` for alternatives and `*` as the catch-all. It's the clean way to branch many ways on one value, where a pile of `if`/`elif` would sprawl.
